name: Jenny Bakery
intro: Hong Kong's cult butter cookies, sold in the teddy-bear tins every visitor is asked to bring home.
tips: Cash only, curt service and popular flavours can sell out by early afternoon, so go before lunch; avoid the look-alike resellers next door. If you can't make Sheung Wan, Cookies Quartet (opposite Causeway Bay MTR Exit F1, card-friendly, also at the airport) is the easy alternative.
address_en: G/F, Wo Hing Commercial Building, 15 Wing Wo Street, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong
address_zh: 香港上環永和街15號和興商業大廈地下

name: Kee Wah Bakery
intro: Since 1938, Hong Kong's go-to bakery for beautifully boxed traditional Chinese pastries.
must_order: Egg rolls in a gift tin
tips: A 5-minute walk from The Park Lane; also at Central MTR, ifc mall and several airport shops (incl. airside T1), so you can buy last-minute.
address_en: G/F, Lai Yuen Apartments, 33 Lee Garden Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
address_zh: 香港銅鑼灣利園山道33號麗園大廈地下

name: Wing Wah Cake Shop
intro: Yuen Long bakery founded in 1950, famous for its flaky wife cakes and egg rolls.
tips: Plain no-frills shop; there is also a branch near campus at 532–534 Queen's Road West, Sai Wan (09:30–19:30).
address_en: Shop E, G/F, Pun Tak Building, 478–484 Lockhart Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
address_zh: 香港銅鑼灣駱克道478-484號本德大廈地下E號舖

name: G.O.D. (Goods of Desire)
intro: Witty homegrown lifestyle brand that turns Hong Kong street culture into well-made gifts.
must_order: Tote or pouch with old-HK print
tips: This Lan Kwai Fong store is the flagship; there is a second shop at 48 Hollywood Road and one at the airport. Cards accepted.
address_en: G/F & M/F, Yip Fung Building, 6 D'Aguilar Street, Central, Hong Kong
address_zh: 香港中環德己立街6號業豐大廈地下及閣樓

name: Yiu Fung Store
intro: Tiny 1960s-era Causeway Bay shop piled high with preserved plums, ginger and tangerine peel.
tips: Crowded and Cantonese-speaking; point at what you want and ask for it boxed as a gift. Also has an airport branch.
address_en: G/F, Po Foo Building, 3 Foo Ming Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
address_zh: 香港銅鑼灣富明街3號寶富大廈地下

name: Kowloon Soy Company
intro: Family soy-sauce maker since 1917, selling from a heritage shopfront on Graham Street.
must_order: Preserved eggs or fermented bean curd
tips: Closed Sundays; glass bottles go in checked luggage, wrapped well.
address_en: G/F, 9 Graham Street, Central, Hong Kong
address_zh: 香港中環嘉咸街9號地下

name: Lam Kie Yuen Tea Co.
intro: Old-school Sheung Wan tea merchant selling loose-leaf Chinese teas and ready-made gift tins.
must_order: Jasmine or Dragon Well green tea
tips: Closed Sundays and public holidays; ask for teas to be packed in gift tins.
address_en: G/F, Lee Man Commercial Building, 105–107 Bonham Strand, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong
address_zh: 香港上環文咸東街105-107號利文商業大廈地下

name: Chinese Arts & Crafts
intro: Since 1959, Hong Kong's classic one-stop store for Chinese silk, jade, porcelain and handicrafts.
tips: Prices are high but quality is reliable, which matters for jade; a short taxi ride from the hotel.
address_en: Shops 2 & 7, G/F, Causeway Centre, 28 Harbour Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
address_zh: 香港灣仔港灣道28號灣景中心大廈地下2及7號舖

name: Shanghai Tang
intro: Hong Kong's original luxury 'Chinese chic' label, good for upscale gifts for clients or a partner.
tips: The old Duddell Street 'Mansion' flagship is no longer listed; the main city store is now in Pacific Place, with another at the airport (T1 East Hall).
address_en: Shop 105B, Level 1, Pacific Place One, 88 Queensway, Admiralty, Hong Kong
address_zh: 香港金鐘道88號太古廣場一期1樓105B號舖
